questions.question: Before evacuating a bus due to a hazard, a driver should:

options.text: Ask the students if they want to leave.
Tell the dispatcher what is happening.
Take time to decide if evacuation is needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell the dispatcher what is happening.
questions.explanation: If there is time, the driver should contact the dispatcher before evacuating the bus. The decision to evacuate must be made quickly.

questions.question: When a school bus is approaching a bus stop, the driver should:

options.text: Not use the mirrors.
Slow down and be careful.
Drive fast and stop suddenly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be careful.
questions.explanation: School bus drivers should approach stops slowly and carefully.

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection test, you do NOT need to:

options.text: Show where the dipstick is located.
Show that the engine oil is at a safe level.
Show that the oil is below the refill mark.

questions.correctAnswerText: Show that the oil is below the refill mark.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, you must show where the dipstick is and that the oil level is safe and above the refill mark. You should not show oil that is below the refill mark.

questions.question: When students are boarding a school bus, the driver should:

options.text: Read a book.
Watch all mirrors.
Only look at the students.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch all mirrors.
questions.explanation: While students board, the driver should watch all mirrors to see if any students are running to catch the bus.

questions.question: The inside rearview mirror is used to:

options.text: Watch passengers inside the bus.
See hazards on the road ahead.
See vehicles changing lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch passengers inside the bus.
questions.explanation: The overhead inside rearview mirror in a school bus is used to watch what passengers are doing inside the bus.

questions.question: During the driving test, the examiner will score you on:

options.text: Your attitude.
How fast you reach your destination.
Your driving behavior overall.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your driving behavior overall.
questions.explanation: During the driving test, the examiner scores you on specific driving moves and your general driving behavior.

questions.question: During the basic control skills test, you will lose points if you:

options.text: Pull up once.
Check your positioning.
Cross over exercise boundaries.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cross over exercise boundaries.
questions.explanation: The examiner counts how many times your vehicle touches or crosses a boundary line. Each touch or crossing is an error and counts against your score.

questions.question: When making a turn during your driving test, you should:

options.text: Use your turn signal only if other cars are nearby.
Check traffic only in the direction you are turning.
Check traffic in all directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check traffic in all directions.
questions.explanation: When making a turn during the driving test, check traffic in all directions and use your turn signal.

questions.question: To safely unload a bus, students should:

options.text: Stay seated until the driver tells them to exit.
Stand up and go toward the door while the bus is slowing down.
Exit and stand next to the bus while it is being driven away.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay seated until the driver tells them to exit.
questions.explanation: Students should stay seated until the driver says it is safe to exit. After exiting, they should walk at least 10 feet away from the bus so the driver can see them clearly.

questions.question: When you reach railroad tracks while driving a school bus, you should:

options.text: Look at the tracks and keep driving without stopping.
Stop 15 to 50 feet before the nearest rail.
Stop 75 feet before the nearest rail.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop 15 to 50 feet before the nearest rail.
questions.explanation: School bus drivers should stop before railroad crossings to check for trains. Stop at least 15 feet but no more than 50 feet from the rail. Look and listen for trains before crossing.

questions.question: What may you be asked to do during a basic vehicle control skills test?

options.text: Swerve to avoid a hazard.
Parallel park.
Drive straight into a parking space.

questions.correctAnswerText: Parallel park.
questions.explanation: The basic vehicle control skills test may include straight line backing, offset back parking, parallel parking, and alley docking.

questions.question: What happens if your vehicle's ABS breaks?

options.text: You will not have any working brakes.
You will still have brakes.
You should only use the parking brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will still have brakes.
questions.explanation: ABS stops your wheels from locking up during hard braking. If your ABS breaks, your regular brakes still work. Drive and brake normally.

questions.question: Where should your vehicle be positioned at the end of a basic vehicle control skills test exercise?

options.text: In the general area the examiner described.
In the exact position the examiner described.
Within three feet of the position the examiner described.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the exact position the examiner described.
questions.explanation: Your vehicle must finish in the exact position the examiner described. Failing to do so can result in losing points or failing the test.

questions.question: If your driving test route does not include a railroad crossing, what may happen?

options.text: You will not have to do anything related to a crossing.
The examiner may ask you to explain how you would cross railroad tracks.
You will have to take a different route.

questions.correctAnswerText: The examiner may ask you to explain how you would cross railroad tracks.
questions.explanation: If your test route has no railroad crossing, the examiner may ask you to explain and show how you would handle one at a practice location.

questions.question: How should students board a school bus?

options.text: In a single-file line.
In pairs.
Without using the handrail.

questions.correctAnswerText: In a single-file line.
questions.explanation: Students should board slowly in a single-file line and use the handrail for safety.

questions.question: What should you do when asked to change lanes during your driving test?

options.text: You should not worry about other drivers.
Use your turn signal and change lanes when it is safe.
Change lanes as quickly as possible, even if it means cutting off another driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your turn signal and change lanes when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors and blind spots, use your turn signal, and smoothly change lanes only when it is safe.

questions.question: Where is the safest place for students during a school bus evacuation?

options.text: No more than 50 feet from the bus.
Downwind of the bus in case of a fire.
Far away from any railroad tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Far away from any railroad tracks.
questions.explanation: After evacuation, lead students at least 100 feet away from the road in the direction of oncoming traffic. Keep them upwind of fires and as far as possible from railroad tracks.

questions.question: Why should a bus driver stop at least 10 feet away from waiting students?

options.text: Students will walk to the bus, making it easier to see their movements.
Buses are difficult to drive.
Students may get scared of the approaching bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Students will walk to the bus, making it easier to see their movements.
questions.explanation: Stopping 10 feet away forces students to walk toward the bus. This lets the driver watch their movements for safety.

questions.question: When should a school bus's roof-mounted strobe light be used?

options.text: When visibility is limited.
All the time.
Only at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: When visibility is limited.
questions.explanation: Use the roof-mounted strobe light when visibility is poor.

questions.question: What should properly adjusted flat mirrors on a school bus show?

options.text: The sides of the school bus.
The ground under the school bus.
The front tires touching the ground.

questions.correctAnswerText: The sides of the school bus.
questions.explanation: Properly adjusted flat mirrors should let the driver see 200 feet behind the bus, the base of each rear wheel, and the sides of the bus.
